newsitem.title: USA: Sales of used homes down slightly in August.
newsitem.headline: Sales of used homes down slightly in August.

text.p: Sales of existing homes eased in August for a third month in a row, the National Association of Realtors said Wednesday, though not enough to suggest a sharp decline in the housing market.

The real estate lobby group said sales of existing, or used, homes fell 0.5 percent in August to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 4.13 million. That followed a revised decline of 0.2 percent to 4.15 million in July and a sharper 2.8 percent drop in June sales.
Resales of used homes exceeded four million a year for six consecutive months through August, a sizzling pace that industry analysts said underlined the durability of the housing sector.
"These numbers are reflecting a very healthy housing market right now," said economist David Lereah of the Mortgage Bankers Association. "According to these numbers, there is no sign of a slowdown."
The real estate agents' group revised upward its estimate of July sales to an annual rate of 4.15 million instead of the 4.14 million it reported a month ago.
A boom in homebuilding and sales helped power the robust 4.8 percent annual rate of expansion in the national economy during the second quarter -- the most vigorous growth in two years.
Sales of existing homes peaked in May at a record rate of 4.28 million a year.

"The nation's housing market is easing in for a soft landing," said John Tuccillo, chief economist for the National Association of Realtors. After the surge in sales earlier in the year, he said, "it's only natural that the market will correct itself."
Economist David Seiders of the National Association of Home Builders said a slowing in housing activity -- both building and sales -- might be welcomed at this point.
Policy-making members of the Federal Reserve decided on Tuesday against raising interest rates, apparently believing the overall economy was cooling on its own enough to keep inflation in check.

"Things are still at a very good level for housing activity but it's pretty clear the pace will be down for the third quarter," Seiders said. "That's probably the way that the Fed saw the housing sector," he added.
The moderate waning in sales of used homes last month occurred despite somewhat cheaper long-term mortgage rates.
The Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp., or Freddie Mac, said the average rate for a 30-year mortgage loan in August was 8 percent, down from July's 8.25 percent average and June's 8.32 percent.

During August, sales of existing homes fell 9.5 percent in the Northeast to 570,000 a year, while in the South, the nation's biggest regional housing market, they were down 1.9 percent to a rate of 1.53 million.
But in the Midwest, August sales edged up 0.9 percent to a rate of 1.07 million a year and in the West they increased strongly, by 5.6 percent to 950,000 a year.
The average price for an existing home resold in August was $149,900, up slightly from $149,600 in July.
